lines: Soviet troops mounted a top secret rocket launcher on a sledge.
But the artillery branch was not fond of the Katyusha.
It took up to 50 minutes to load and fire 24 rounds.
A normal howitzer could fire 95 to 150 rounds in the same time.
Only forty launchers were built before Germany invaded in June 1941.
On 14 July 1941, Captain Ivan Flyorov commanded a battery of seven launchers at Rudnya.
The rockets destroyed German troops, tanks and trucks in the marketplace.
Their howling sound terrified the German troops.
They called the weapon Stalin's organ.
But the launcher was fragile compared to artillery guns.
It had to deliver a large blow all at once.
Then it had to move before the enemy located it.
You see, it's like a backpack.
It doesn't care whose back carries it.
The Katyusha was cheap, easy to produce, and usable on almost any chassis.
It rode on trucks, tractors, tanks, armoured trains and river boats.
And on towed sledges.
The launchers were marked with the letter K.
So Red Army troops borrowed a name from a wartime song.
It was about a woman longing for her absent beloved.
The song was called Katyusha.

claims.claim: The multiple rocket launchers were top secret at the beginning of World War II; chassis for the launchers included a towed sledge.
The artillery branch was not fond of the Katyusha, because it took up to 50 minutes to load and fire 24 rounds, while a conventional howitzer could fire 95 to 150 rounds in the same time.
Only forty launchers were built before Germany invaded the Soviet Union in June 1941.

On 14 July 1941, an experimental artillery battery of seven launchers was first used in battle at Rudnya under the command of Captain Ivan Flyorov, destroying a concentration of German troops with tanks, armored vehicles and trucks in the marketplace.
German troops coined the nickname Stalin's organ; the weapon's distinctive howling sound terrified the German troops.
They are fragile compared to artillery guns, but are cheap, easy to produce, and usable on almost any chassis.
Mobility let the Katyusha deliver a large blow all at once, and then move before being located and attacked with counter-battery fire.
Chassis for the launchers included trucks, an artillery tractor, a tank, an armored train car, a river boat and a towed sledge.
Because they were marked with the letter K, Red Army troops adopted a nickname from the popular wartime song Katyusha, about a woman longing for her absent beloved.

cast.german: a 24 year old German soldier with a thin pale face, sunken blue eyes, a grey steel helmet and a grey-green wool greatcoat, 1940s
cast.woman: a 25 year old Russian village woman with long dark braids, rosy cheeks, a red flowered headscarf and a white embroidered linen blouse, 1940s
